# Charter — SPEC-V2 (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

- **Project:** SPEC-V2 'SPEC V2 — the organisational operating model', project `01a1d039-0d39-7f3b-bd04-211f7dfe1e50`, track programme, ADM phase Preliminary, plateau definition, tranche 0. The facts brief records the project closed; the rework note records the closure on 2026-11-17. It was reopened for the retrospective MSP/TOGAF/SAFe rework of tranche 0 (#526), and this pack re-closes it through the one gate. Plan `docs/SPEC_V2.md`, active; the row's measured status is `built` and its viability is `rework`.
- **Mandate:** give the conveyor an organisation it owns — industry → department(s) → job, an immutable job release, a tenant-scoped binding and a recorded decision trail — and publish it as the `spec` output, with the seven Phase A–D artefacts approved by the Architecture Board and one accepted WBS deliverable.
- **Scope:** the plan and its decision set, the seven A–D artefacts, the delivery contract, the scope baseline, the Phase-G review and the closure record. Out of scope: V1's S-slices (not re-opened), the V2 delivery slices T0–T19 and T19F (their own projects), and `docs/SPEC_LEGACY_KAG.md` (D54).
- **Delegation and date:** authored retrospectively on 2026-11-26 under the #526 rework delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`. It records a completed lifecycle; it authorises no new work and claims no certification (§8.6).
- **Honest residual:** who closed the project on 2026-11-17 and why is not recoverable — no approval row and no closure asset survive — so this charter states the closure without inventing a decision-maker, and it does not restate the contemporaneous WSJF inputs as if they had been recovered.

body.assignment: Rework SPEC-V2 by the reconstituted TOGAF/MSP lifecycle: author the charter, this Statement of Architecture Work, the seven Phase A–D artefacts and the eight Phase E–H artefacts, the delivery contract, the WBS deliverable and the Phase-G review, and publish the `spec` output. The plan is `docs/SPEC_V2.md` — the organisational operating model that gives the conveyor its own industry → department(s) → job spine, work hierarchy, decision ladder and executable rigour. The work is retrospective and dated 2026-11-26; the live statement it re-versions is `01a1ff41-19f9-77bb-aa4a-f416f0d758e3`.
body.scope: The V2 document and its decisions, together with the architecture artefacts the delivery contract governs: the stakeholder map, the driver/goal/objective catalogue, the requirements catalogue and the solution concept (phase A); the business capability map (phase B); the data entity/data component catalogue (phase C); the technology standards catalogue (phase D); and the eight E–H deliverables this pack authors. Not in scope: V1's S-slices, the V2 delivery slices T0–T19 and T19F, and `docs/SPEC_LEGACY_KAG.md` (D54).

The acceptance manifest `acceptance/programme/SPEC-V2.toml` is green: the closure review exists, the declared `spec` output is published, and the project re-closes through the one gate decided by an approver other than its requester. The seven A–D artefacts are approved rows with their entries; the live Phase-G review `01a1ff43-a1bc-758d-89dc-c97d0fb0265a` records exactly one level, compliant, against the delivery contract `01a1ff42-7bd0-7d9e-883a-1059368cd356`.

The matrix carries eight positions. The programme owner and sponsor decides whether the model is adopted and its gates hold. The Architecture Board approves contracts and artefacts (D63, §8.1). The maintainer sessions are consulted because the conveyor develops and operates itself under its own gates (D34, P7). The five first departments — delivery, verification, operations, project office and improvement — are consulted (§4.6). entries.axis_a: D1 V1 answers how work is carried, not who the organisation is (§1.1)
entries.axis_b: G1 The organisation is a set of configured positions

entries.axis_b: G5 The conveyor owns its whole model and is self-contained

entries.axis_b: G6 PM, coach, kata, development and operations are ordinary jobs

entries.axis_b: G7 Meetings are the decision forum

artifacts.title: Requirements catalog — SPEC-V2 (retrospective, 2026-11-21)
artifacts.purpose: State the requirements the operating model must meet, typed as the standard requires.
artifacts.scope: The invariants of §3, the binding decisions D28–D66 and the amendments V2 makes to V1.

stakeholders.owner: the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation

value.acceptance: No concept is stored in two systems; systems join by pinned reference (P1, §10.1).
No work without a card; no transition without an action; no completion without evidence (P3).

entries.axis_b: The executor never approves its own work

value.acceptance: Dual control on gates, `decided_by_kind`, and an approver who is neither the assignee nor the executor (P4).
An unresolved binding, pack, prompt source or tool refuses `409 *_not_ready` with `blocking[]` before the first model call or action (P8).

entries.axis_b: Every model call is ledgered and budgeted

value.acceptance: `inference_call` rows with per-run and per-tenant budgets; exceeding a budget is a refusal before the next call (P9, §7.5).
A table exists because a named procedure uses it and a metric reads it; an unused aggregate is removed, not defended (P10, D40).
Every policy, threshold, limit, gate condition and approval kind is a versioned tenant-scoped row with a platform default; code implements mechanisms, never policy values (P11, D50).

entries.axis_b: Immutable releases; a stale binding refuses

value.acceptance: A binding pins `job_key` + `release_hash` + an immutable `release_snapshot`; a run against a retired binding refuses `409 job_binding_stale` before any model call (D38).
Every tool declares one of read, write, destructive or spend; a binding's ceiling narrows only; a destructive call needs a dry-run and the tenant's configured approvals (D45, §11.4).
A benefit without baseline, target, method and owner is refused; the benefits map names output → capability → operational outcome → benefit → objective (D62, §8.3).

entries.axis_b: A delivery project needs its governing contract

value.acceptance: A delivery project cannot pass design without the live contract that governs it; a Phase-G review records exactly one of the six standard levels (D63, §8.1).

entries.axis_b: The agent platform is a front end

value.acceptance: It is a conversation surface over MCP with its own autonomy configuration — not a catalogue, an executor or a system of record for conveyor work (D33, D59).

entries.axis_b: laya answers inside the seam budget

value.acceptance: `POST /v1/systemone`, with the fail policy owned by the decision policy; a timeout never becomes an LLM decision (§7.2, §10.2).
V1 D1–D27 stand except D14 and D22, which V2 amends through D57 and D46/D61; no V1 S-slice is re-opened (Appendix B).

entries.axis_b: Procedural knowledge has no ontology store

value.acceptance: Amended 2026-11-19: RDF/OWL/Turtle is imported as a strata knowledge pack named by the procedure's `knowledge_pack_ref`; the conveyor runs no RDF store, no graph store and no reasoner (D53, §5.6).

Every requirement is typed condition, constraint, assumption or delta, and every requirement, principle and ADR is a governed asset trace-linked to the artefacts, contracts, cards, runs and evidence that realise it (D63, §8.1, §8.5).

artifacts.title: Solution concept — SPEC-V2 (retrospective, 2026-11-21)
artifacts.purpose: Show the building blocks of the operating model and how a decision and a unit of work pass through them.
artifacts.scope: Jobs, releases and bindings, cards and runs, approvals, the decision ladder, the work hierarchy, the broker, the rigour, storage and the executor seam.

stakeholders.owner: the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation

value.note: A capability, a procedure, an inference configuration and an authority — a configured position, not a loop (§2, D28).
The immutable compiled release with a content hash; the binding pins job_key + release_hash + release_snapshot (D38, §4.4).
The unit of assigned work and one recorded attempt; the card and run are the units, not the conversational turn (§2).
The one human-escalation primitive — a question is an approval; dual control is two or more distinct approvers (§5.4).
Rule → laya → generation → human; an LLM never selects, routes, classifies or approves, and a generated draft has no path to a state transition (D30, P2, §7.1).
Tenant → portfolio (a computed read model, never a row) → programme (shared_config + project dependency graph) → project → WBS → card → run → step (D29, D49, §5.1).
Resolve the binding and version, check the effect, validate the closed schema, resolve the credential by alias, call the registered destination, normalise and redact, record one tool_call (§11.3).
The Preliminary phase establishes the principles, tailored ADM, board, repository and baselines; phases A–H are WBS nodes that close on an approved architecture contract (D63, §8.1).
programme_cadence carries PI planning, refinement, demo and retro; programme_tranche is the management unit and its review is an approval (§8.2–§8.3).
Document rows plus MinIO written directly under tenant prefixes with encryption, a content hash and a size cap; there is no artifact_service dependency (D57, §11.10).
Two live kinds — procedure and internal_agent — behind one internal Executor contract with an extensible executor_kind; an external runtime is a non-goal until D61's four conditions hold.
A card whose agenda items resolve existing approvals, with a meeting_type policy row for participation, quorum, decision rule and the closed outcome set; never a fifth unit and never a chat (D66).

stakeholders.owner: the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation

value.usage: One binary, typed actions and compiler-enforced crate boundaries; V2 keeps the Rust substrate V1 built and there is no flow generator (§1.4).
Same binary, same Postgres, same namespace and no new port (8930) (§10.6).
One declaration serving HTTP, MCP, OpenAPI and a generated client (§10.4).
Agent to conveyor only; there is no conveyor-to-agent call, and the tool surface is versioned like an external API (§10.2, D33).
Closed schemas with additionalProperties false, enums, patterns and bounds (§11.3, §11.7).
A draft toolkit with per-operation effect classes and a registered destination alias (D42, §11.5).
Binding-scoped discovery; only the bound subset is exposed to the tenant's jobs (§11.5).
Direct writes under a tenant prefix with server-side encryption, a content hash and a size cap; no artifact_service or storage-api dependency (D57, §11.10).
Pinned-leaf retrieval, knowledge-pack import and cold digests; the conveyor never hosts embeddings (§5.6, §10.1).
POST /v1/systemone behind a Jev-compatible bridge, measured at roughly 17 to 21 ms per request on 2026-10-10; the fail policy is the decision policy's (§7.2).
The action space: preconditions and effects over typed facts; procedural knowledge is the published procedure itself (D53).
Imported into a strata knowledge pack named by the procedure's knowledge_pack_ref; no RDF store, no graph store and no reasoner (D53, amended 2026-11-19).
Activities become steps and gateways become gates; the result is a procedure draft behind a review gate (§5.6, D53).
A lean profile with named artefacts and gates, nine maturity dimensions and seven skills categories; no certification claim (§8.1, §8.6).
As rows and gates; no SAFe compliance badge, PMP certification or MSP conformance badge (§8.2 to §8.4, §8.6).
A viewpoint string on a typed artefact, not a live metamodel and no modelling tool (§8.6).
Read verbs live; destructive verbs behind approval, a dry-run and dual control (§11.2, §11.4).
The broker is in-process and the one internal agent loop is the only runtime (§10.6).

artifacts.scope: Four candidates: V1 plus ad-hoc agents, a field framework, the conveyor-owned model and an external executor runtime.

stakeholders.owner: the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation

entries.axis_a: Keep V1 and add ad-hoc agents

entries.axis_b: a second runtime beside the internal one

value.rationale: D61 makes an external runtime an explicit non-goal until four conditions hold — a generic work-packet ingress with per-step evidence, governance at the boundary, separate owners and roadmaps, and a win on the conveyor's own benchmark. The seam is built in T0 at near-zero cost.

documents.body:
# Project Brief — SPEC-V2 (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Outcome

SPEC-V2 delivers `docs/SPEC_V2.md`, the conveyor's organisational operating model, and publishes it as the `spec` output: an organisation spine of industry → department(s) → job with an immutable release and a tenant-scoped binding, a work hierarchy from programme to run, a four-rung decision ladder, and TOGAF, SAFe, PMP and MSP implemented as rows and gates rather than documents. The outcome the plan states in §13 is that the organisation's work becomes auditable at the level of a single decision — which option, which confidence, which policy, which person, which evidence.

## Boundary

Out of scope are V1's S-slices, which are not re-opened; the V2 delivery slices T0–T19 and T19F, which are their own projects; and `docs/SPEC_LEGACY_KAG.md`, which owns the legacy-kag and w2v rewrites (D54). The model explicitly does not do customer care (D48), does not import a manifest from another system (D33), and does not claim TOGAF certification, SAFe compliance, PMP certification, MSP conformance or full ADM conformance (§8.6).

## Reuse sources

The plan reuses the ideas of the agent platform's KH model (D106–D115) and reimplements them, so there is no runtime import (D33). It reuses V1's Rust substrate, its capability → procedure → step → action or gate knowledge, its run, approval, action_invocation and event memory, its capability_agent executor configuration, its inference ledger and its eval and benchmark instruments. The retrospective record reuses the snapshot's approved A–D rows and the rework note's residuals.

## Inception units

The delivery units are the V2 slices: T0 to T3 and T13 in the first three months, T4 to T12 and T14 to T19 as the following work, and T19F as the measured follow-on (§12). The retrospective reconstitution of this project's own lifecycle is the #526 unit, whose 38 acts are recorded in `transcript.jsonl` and read back one write at a time by `programme-record.py`. Units T9 and T10 are measured built on 2026-11-23, and T19F on 2026-11-24.

## Dependencies

Every delivery slice depends on the T0 spine and, from T6 and T7 onward, on the T13 tool spine (§12). The decision ladder depends on laya, live on the DGX behind a Jev-compatible bridge on :9210 at roughly 17 to 21 ms per request measured 2026-10-10. # Benefits Diagram — SPEC-V2 (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Goals and outcomes

The goal is an organisation the conveyor owns and can prove: positions that are catalogued, released and bound; work that moves from programme to run with a baseline, a register and evidence; and decisions that pass rule → laya → generation → human with every step recorded. The measurable outcome is auditability at the level of a single decision — which option, which confidence, which policy, which person, which evidence (§13). The plan calls this the unglamorous win, and it is the outcome the benefit depends on.

## Measures

The measures are computed read models, never stored opinions (D37): flow (lead time, cycle time, queue time, block time, flow efficiency, WIP, throughput), quality (first-pass yield, rework rate, defect escapes, eval score, benchmark delta), cost from the ledger, governance (gate latency, approval rate, override rate, evidence completeness, never-refused gates) and knowledge (pack hit rate, citation rate, readiness blocks, lesson promotion). Metering rolls up at tenant, department, programme, project and job and drills to run, step and call, reconciled with billing_service (D52). A gate that never refused in a full cycle is flagged as broken.

## Benefits and sub-benefits

The benefit is auditability at the level of a single decision. Its sub-benefits are a staffed improvement loop — coach, kata, development, measurement and adoption as one loop (§9.4); a programme cadence in which a PI is the delivery rhythm and a tranche is the managed unit, with the review an approval carrying baselines, benefit status and the risk register (§8.2, §8.3); and executable rigour, with TOGAF, SAFe, PMP and MSP as rows and gates and no certification claim (§8.6). A benefit without baseline, target, method and owner is refused, so no sub-benefit can be claimed on a wish.

# Candidate Solutions — SPEC-V2 (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Candidates

Four routes were considered. The first keeps V1 and adds ad-hoc agents, which preserves the working machine and leaves the organisation, cadence and meta-jobs absent. The second adopts a field framework — CrewAI, ChatDev/DevAll or n8n — and inherits their conversation model. The third is V2 as specified: the conveyor owns the whole model in four units, with typed rows and gates. The fourth adds an external executor runtime beside the internal one, and D61 defers it until four stated conditions hold.

## Criteria

The routes are judged on five criteria the plan already fixes: one record per fact (P1), so no concept is stored twice; no speculative aggregate (P10), so a table exists only because a named procedure uses it and a metric reads it; tenant configuration over code (P11), so policies are versioned rows; self-containment (D33), so the conveyor owns its model and the agent platform is a front end; and measurement before adoption (P5), so a change is adopted because a held-out instrument moved. A sixth, narrower criterion is honesty of claim: no certification or conformance badge (§8.6).

## Options rejected

Keeping V1 and adding ad-hoc agents is rejected because the organisation spine, the programme cadence, the meta-jobs and the operations perspective do not exist, and the improvement loop has nothing staffing it. The field frameworks are rejected because they build agent conversations, while organisations run on positions, work products, gates, baselines and evidence; the measured n8n estate — 348 workflows, 280 of them the generated card-type by list matrix, each with its own error exits — is the plan's own caution (§1.3, §1.4). The external runtime is deferred, not rejected: D61 names the four conditions, and the seam in T0 preserves the option at near-zero cost.

# Spec — SPEC-V2 (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Context

V1 built one Rust application that carries work: projects, boards, lists, cards, runs, approvals, procedures, capabilities, capability agents, knowledge and memory bindings, an inference ledger, a native SWE-bench harness, evals and the compiled-prompt pipeline. Its last whole-tree checkpoint of 2026-11-09 measured 83 tables and 243 actions as a floor, and the app is live at `conveyor.nonagentic.ai` on main `85487a04`, 3 pods, with `/health` and `/health/ready` 200 on `:8930` (deploy record 2026-11-10). V1 answers how work is carried; it does not answer who the organisation is. Three independently built things — the `agent` platform as a user of the conveyor over MCP, the KH hierarchy proving positions, departments and immutable releases, and the conveyor's own work and proof rows — have arrived at the same shape, and the missing piece is the organisation. The field builds agent conversations; real organisations run on positions, work products, gates, baselines and evidence.

## Requirements

The requirements are the plan's hard invariants and its binding decisions. One record per fact: no concept is stored in two systems, and systems join by pinned reference. No work without a card; no transition without an action; no completion without evidence. The executor never approves its own work, and dual control is two or more distinct approvers. Rule → laya → generation → human: an LLM never selects, routes, classifies or approves, and a generated output is a draft with no path to a state transition. Every model call is ledgered and budgeted; an unresolved binding, pack, prompt source or tool fails closed with `409 *_not_ready` before the first call. No speculative aggregate: a table exists because a named procedure uses it and a metric reads it. Tenant configuration over code: every policy, threshold, limit and approval kind is a versioned tenant-scoped row with a platform default. Requirements are typed condition, constraint, assumption or delta and are managed continuously, not by phase.

## Design

The design has four units and nothing else: a job (a position — a capability, a procedure, an inference configuration and an authority), a card (a work package), an approval (the one human-escalation primitive, where a question is an approval) and a run (one recorded attempt). Departments, programmes and portfolios organise them; knowledge, memory and tools configure them; evals, benchmarks and the ledger measure them; a meeting is a decision forum over them. The organisation spine is industry → department(s), ordered → job, with knowledge layered base → industry → department archetype → each department in order → job, compiled into an immutable release; a binding pins `job_key`, `release_hash` and a `release_snapshot`, and a retired binding refuses `409 job_binding_stale` before any model call. The work hierarchy is tenant → portfolio (computed, never a row) / programme (shared_config plus project dependency edges) → project → WBS → card → run → step. TOGAF ADM, SAFe, PMP and MSP are rows and gates: phases are WBS nodes, artefacts are typed rows with entries and links, gates are approvals, tranches are the programme's management unit, and a benefit without baseline, target, method and owner is refused. The tool estate is a catalogue of immutable toolkit versions, a binding with an effect ceiling and one `tool_call` row per call, all through one in-process broker; bytes go directly to MinIO under tenant prefixes.

## Acceptance

The acceptance is executable. `python3 scripts/verify-project.py --project SPEC-V2 --snapshot <fresh>` is green with 11 checks and 0 failures at `d7293f96`, the strict audit on the same snapshot carries no P0/P1 entry, and the acceptance manifest `acceptance/programme/SPEC-V2.toml` is the gate's evidence. The seven A–D artefacts are approved rows published 2026-11-22 and the eight E–H artefacts are authored on 2026-11-26; the Phase-G review records level compliant; the project re-closes through the one gate with an approver other than its requester. The plan's own slice acceptance is narrower and testable: T0 proves that a job is created, a release published, a binding pinned and a run on a retired binding refused; later slices each carry a named refusal. No TOGAF certification, SAFe compliance badge, PMP certification, MSP conformance or full ADM conformance is claimed, and that restraint is part of the acceptance.
